_about: Every material in the world, and what happens when two of them touch.
Ids are fixed: the game refers to them. Add new materials with new ids (up to 255).
kind: empty | static (never moves) | powder (falls and piles) | liquid (falls and spreads) | gas (rises or sinks).
density: heavier powders and liquids sink through lighter liquids and gases; gases sort themselves by it too.
Liquids: look = how far a surface cell looks sideways for a drop, max_step = how far it moves in a tick,
wander_bits = a still surface cell wanders 1 tick in 2^bits, slow = only moves every Nth tick.
Gases: buoyancy -8..8 = rises (+) or sinks (-), moving |b|/8 of its updates; drift = sideways moves in 256.
stages = how many ids it ages through (from its id up), age_chance = ages 1 update in N,
condenses_to = what the last stage becomes (expires_alt instead, with alt_chance), vents = vanishes at the top of the map.
life [min, max] = updates it lasts (life_decay = chance per update of using one up), then it
becomes expires_to, or expires_alt with alt_chance.
Statics: loosens_to = what it becomes with nothing under or beside it, erodes_to = what exposed cells
slowly turn into, crumbles_to = what tremors turn it into, crumble = chance a cell hanging over open
space comes away when weathering checks it (it falls as crumbles_into).
Collapse: span = widest open run (air, gas or liquid) under a ceiling of it that stands; wider and
it caves in from the middle, falling as crumbles_into, until what's left is within overhang
cells of the run's ends (an arch). No span: it never caves in. cave = chance each sweep (about 3 a
second) that a cell that should come down does (default 1/3). cohesive: it hangs only from its
own kind (or rock with no span): counted along the row, other ground beside it doesn't hold it.
Water: wash_to / wash = what a cell touching water (any liquid that isn't hot) wears into, and the
chance each time the wash pass checks it (Air: washed away).
Blasts: durability = what a blast must beat to break it (255 = never); shatters_to = what a broken
static flies off as (powders and liquids fly off as themselves).
burn: life = how long a cell burns, ignite = chance something hot lights it when it checks it,
speed = chance per update of burning down one step, to = what it leaves, gas / gas_chance and
flame_chance = what it gives off into open space as it burns. Fire needs air: a burning cell
with no open side stops spreading and soon goes out.
flame: the fire burning things throw off. hot: lights what burns, and burns buildings it touches.
quench: puts out burning neighbours, turning into quench_to. corrosive: eats buildings and links nearby.
scalds: hurts Nodes it wraps. glows: lights up the rock around it.
Temperature (A1): every cell has one, in degrees; a slow pass leaks heat between neighbours. conduct =
how readily heat crosses into a neighbour (0..1; default by kind: rock 0.2, powder 0.12, liquid 0.4,
gas and air 0.04; a pair takes the lower), sink = how strongly the depth's ambient pulls the cell
back (rock 1, powder 0.25, else 0). temp = what a cell arrives at when placed from outside (water
is cold wherever it's put; without it, the spot's). hold = a source keeps itself at this (lava), closing hold_rate
of the gap a pass; burn.temp = the same while it burns. heats {at, to, cost} = above `at` it becomes
`to`, spending `cost` degrees (water boils); cools {at, to, cost} = below `at` (hot rock to stone;
lava to obsidian). kindle = catches fire at this with an open side.
family: one tag or a list (Fuel, Corrosive, Molten, ...). Reactions can name a family on either side
and stand for every pair of its members; a reaction written for a material pair overrides them.
'same' in becomes keeps that side. min_temp / max_temp = the first cell's degrees must be within;
heat = degrees both outputs gain; catalyst = a family that, touching, multiplies the chance by boost.
Wave 1 (A2): heat_mass = how many cells' worth of heat it takes to move its temperature (Rime 20).
sets {to, speed, catalyst, boost} = a countdown in aux (it starts from `life`), a step with chance `speed` an update
(boost times as often beside a cell of the catalyst family); at zero the cell becomes `to`. blast {radius, power,
impact, temp, flame, inhibit} = goes off (a blast, and the like of it within the radius a few ticks later) on a landing
faster than `impact` cells a second, at `temp` degrees, or with fire beside it (`flame`), unless a cell of the
`inhibit` family touches it. absorbs {to, chance} = beside a liquid it and that cell become `to`, which keeps the
liquid's id in aux; bursts {at, into} = a swollen cell over `at` degrees turns into the plume of what it soaked
(a liquid's `plume`), else `into`. grows {over, feed, reach, chance} = takes over a neighbour in `over` when a
cell of the `feed` family is within `reach` cells (that cell is used up). body {w, h} = what a reaction's `emit`
forges: a rigid body of that size beside the cell. burn.catalyst / burn.boost = burns down boost times as fast beside

that family; ages_exposed = a gas that ages (and stays awake) only with open air beside it; burn.wet = keeps burning beside water (only a liquid that turns into something puts it out; Hush still does).
A reaction with chance 0 blocks the family rule it would match without doing anything.
Light: light = glows by itself, radius in cells (burning cells glow like Fire). opacity = how many cells
of air light loses crossing one cell of it (default: open 1, liquid 2, solid 5). structure: a
building's cells, clear to light and not ground to anchor on.
Digging: dig_rate = cells of depth a second at full pace, dig_power = power per cell, yields = the
stockpile(s) it goes to when dug or swallowed (a list gives one unit of each), worth = units a
cell pays against dirt's 1 (world deposits: 6, so their supply keeps up with v2's since the rescale).
good (A5) = a pixel of it banks as a good, a count of units kept under its own id (worth = units a cell pays),
not into one of the five stockpiles; a Funnel or Bus Hopper banks it, a Bus Hopper can spit it back out.
casts_to (A5) = the solid a Caster sets a liquid into, one cell of block for one cell of liquid. fuel (A5) = power a Combustor gets from burning one cell.
Drawing: color, color2 and accent are hex colours; style = empty | flat | rock | strata | speckle |
sparkle | water | lava | fade | smoke | fire; grain = per-cell brightness jitter; mix = the style's
own number (speckle: how rare color2 is; fade: how see-through, first to last stage; smoke: how thick).
rock: counts as rock for the heat warning. glints: shows through the fog now and then.
sensed: outlined when a Cutter feels it hidden nearby.
sighted: the note shown the first time one is seen. kin: another material that counts as its own
kind for cohesive (hot rock hangs from stone and stone from hot rock).
Reactions: when the two materials in 'when' touch, they become the two in 'becomes' (same order),
with 'chance' per update of either cell (1 = always).

materials.name: Fire
materials.sighted: Fire. Burning coal throws flames; water puts it out. Fire wrecks buildings and breaks links.

materials.name: Coal
materials.sighted: Coal. Digging it banks Stone and Power. It burns: keep lava and flames off it.

materials.name: Sulfur
materials.sighted: Sulfur. Worth Stone and Glimmer, but it eats buildings and links near it, and burns into fumes.

materials.name: Sulfur fumes
materials.sighted: Sulfur fumes. They sink and pool, corroding what they touch, and thin out after a while.

materials.name: Packed dirt
materials.sighted: Packed dirt. Slow to dig, and it roofs over wide rooms without caving in.

materials.name: Gravel
materials.sighted: Gravel. It won't roof anything wider than 40 and comes down fast, but water doesn't touch it.

materials.name: Sand
materials.sighted: Sand. It pours the moment it's opened up, and water slowly carries it off.

materials.name: Clay
materials.sighted: Clay. Water doesn't wear it; it lines the aquifers.

materials.name: Hot rock
materials.sighted: Hot rock. The Drill and Borers need the Coolant Jacket to cut it, mites need Ember Brood. Water boils on it, and enough of it cools the surface to stone.

materials.name: Slick
materials.sighted: Slick. Oil: it floats on water and burns for a long time.

materials.name: Sourwater
materials.sighted: Sourwater. Water that eats stone and metal, and the buildings and links beside it. Glass and crystal ignore it.

materials.name: Hush
materials.sighted: Hush. A heavy gas that pools on cave floors and puts out any fire it touches.

materials.name: Quickmire
materials.sighted: Quickmire. Cement: loose ground it touches sets into stone in about ten seconds.

materials.name: Flux
materials.sighted: Flux. A pale powder that speeds up reactions beside it and is never used up. Smelting needs it.

materials.name: Ferrite
materials.sighted: Ferrite. Dense red ore that carries heat well. With Flux and enough heat it smelts into bars.

materials.name: Rattle
materials.sighted: Rattle. A powder that goes off when it lands hard, gets hot or meets fire, and sets off the Rattle beside it.

materials.name: Bloat
materials.sighted: Bloat. A dry puffball that soaks up liquid and swells. Heat bursts it.

materials.name: Glass
materials.sighted: Glass. Light passes through it, acid doesn't touch it, and a hard fall shatters it to sand.

materials.name: Rime
materials.sighted: Rime. Far below freezing and slow to warm: it freezes water, quenches lava to obsidian, and melts away doing it.

materials.name: Wisp
materials.sighted: Wisp. A faintly glowing gas that flashes into flame and a small blast at the first spark.

materials.name: Weft
materials.sighted: Weft. A fungus that turns the dirt and sand beside it into more of itself, drinking any water nearby. Dig it out.
